title: Let Sinners Take Their Course
description: Let Sinners Take Their Course in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 55, part 2, headed “Dangerous prosperity; or, Daily devotions encouraged”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let sin-ners take their course, And choose the road to death; But in the wor-ship of my God I'll spend my dail-y breath.

lines: And choose the road to death;
But in the worship of my God
I seek his blessing every noon,
And pay my vows at night.
They neither fear nor trust thy Name,
Nor learn to do thy will.
But I with all my cares
I'll cast my burdens on his arm,
The ground on which their safety stands

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
